subject: Re: Negative cache kickoff — mid-scale results
body:
Hi both,

Mid-scale comparison is done. Summary:

- Quality: cache-based training matches our current negative sampler on benchmark A (recall@10 0.842 vs 0.845, inside noise) and beats it on benchmark B (+1.9 points recall@10). The score_transform scaling (20x, per the release) mattered — without it the cache loss underweights hard negatives early in training.
- Cost: 38% less accelerator time to reach the quality plateau. That's the headline for the adoption guide.
- Staleness ablation: quality is flat until cache embeddings are ~4k steps stale, then degrades quickly. Our June config refreshes well inside that, so I'm comfortable.

Risk for June: the current sampler arm at full corpus size needs the brute-force miner, which is memory-hungry on H100s — Oyin is validating it fits at 256 accelerators alongside the cache arm's schedule. If it doesn't, we stagger the arms within the week rather than shrink the corpus.

Freya
